newsitem.title: USA: US budget amendment foes have momentum - Sen Daschle.
newsitem.headline: US budget amendment foes have momentum - Sen Daschle.

text.p: Senate Democratic Leader Tom Daschle said Tuesday momentum was continuing to run against passage of a balanced budget constitutional amendment.

"Momentum is on our side," Daschle, of South Dakota, told reporters. The vote is considered too close to call and will probably depend on two undecided Democrats, Mary Landrieu of Louisiana and Robert Torricelli of New Jersey. Landrieu said Monday she was having doubts about the amendment.
The amendment needs a two-thirds majority, or 67 of the 100 senators. Daschle said he thought a final vote would come sometime next week.
If the balanced budget amendment passes the Senate, it would also face a difficult fight in the House, where opponents have blocked it in the House Judiciary Committee.

President Clinton opposes the amendment, but cannot veto it. However, even if a constitutional amendment passes both chambers of Congress, it would not take effect unless it was also passed by three-fourths of the state legislatures of the 50 U.S. states.
